Other possible answer:- Authorities/they/people believe that company has acquired the land illegally through forged documents.

questions.question:
Change passive to active.
Rare minerals are known to have been secretly extracted from the site by unauthorized workers before the inspection.
options: (a) Unauthorized workers extracted the rare minerals before inspection.
(b) The site was secretly mined before the inspection.
(c) Unauthorized workers are known to have secretly extracted rare minerals before inspection.
(d) The minerals had been extracted prior to inspection.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c)
Explanation:- Sentence ko passive to active karna hai, isliye 'are known' aur 'have been secretly extracted' mein se ek bhi agar active mein ho jaaye toh sahi hoga kyunki isme best option nahi hai. Option A, B aur D isliye galat honge kyunki inme galat past indefinite tense aur D mein past perfect tense ka use hua hai, lekin sentence mein present tense ki baat ki hai. Option C sahi hoga kyunki 'have been secretly extracted' perfect tense ko active mein 'have secretly extracted' mein change kar diya aur 'are known' passive mein hee chod diya, agar ek verb bhi active mein ho jaaye toh yeh structure bhi sahi hota hai.
Other possible answer:- Authorities/they/people know that unauthorized workers have extracted rare minerals before inspection.

questions.question:
Change passive to active.
The draft is understood to have been reviewed by the legal department last week.
options: (a) The legal department is understood to have reviewed the draft last week.
(b) The draft was reviewed last week, as is understood.
(c) It was understood the legal team is reviewing the draft.
(d) The draft understood itself to be reviewed.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Sentence ko passive to active karna hai, isliye 'is understood' aur 'have been reviewed' mein se ek bhi agar active mein ho jaaye toh sahi hoga kyunki isme best option nahi hai. Option B, C aur D isliye galat honge kyunki inme galat past indefinite tense use kiya hai, lekin sentence mein present tense ki baat ki hai. Option A sahi hoga kyunki 'have been reviewed' perfect tense ko active mein 'have reviewed' mein change kar diya aur 'is understood' passive mein hee chod diya, toh ek verb bhi agar active mein ho jaaye toh yeh structure bhi sahi hota hai.
Other possible answer:- They/people understand that the legal department had reviewed/reviewed the draft last week. (had reviewed/reviewed isliye kyunki 'last week' ke sath past tense ka use hota hai).

questions.question:
Change passive to active.
The investigation was believed to have been compromised by internal leaks.
options: (a) The investigation compromised internal leaks, as believed.
(b) It was believed that internal leaks had compromised the investigation.
(c) Someone believed the investigation was compromising leaks.
(d) Internal leaks are believed to compromise the investigation.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Sentence ko passive to active karna hai, isliye 'was believed' aur 'have been compromised' mein se ek bhi agar active mein ho jaaye toh sahi hoga kyunki isme best option nahi hai. Option D galat hoga kyunki isse present tense mein change kar diya. Option C bhi galat hoga kyunki 'have been compromised' perfect tense ko 'was compromising' past continuous mein change kar diya. Option A bhi galat hoga kyunki perfect tense ko past tense mein change kar diya. Option B chal jayega kyunki sentence past ka hai aur investigation compromised pehle hui hogi, isliye present perfect ko past perfect mein change kar sakte hai, isliye 'had compromised' sahi hoga aur 'was believed' ko passive mein hee chod diya, agar do verb mein se ek bhi active mein ho jaaye yaa tense ke according change ho jaaye toh yeh structure sahi hota hai.

questions.question:
Change passive to active.
The decision was expected to be made by the council after further review.
options: (a) The council expected making a decision after review.
(b) It was expected that the council would make the decision after review.
(c) The council made the decision as was expected.
(d) The council was expected to have made the decision.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Sentence mein 'was expected' aur 'to be made' passive mein hai agar ek bhi verb active mein ho jaaye toh sahi ho jayega kyunki best option nahi hai. Option B sahi hoga kyunki 'to be made' ko 'would make' active mein change kar diya, yahan 'would' ka use meaning ke according kiya hai kyunki 'had' likhne se matlab hoga unhone expect kar liya tha, lekin 'expect' mein cheezein future mein hoti hai, isliye yahan 'would make' sahi hai aur isliye yeh structure bhi chal jayega.
Other Possible Answer:- 1. Yaa toh dono active ho jaaye 2. Yaa dono mein koi ek active ho jaaye 3. Yaa 'it' introductory subject lagake ek verb ko meaning ke according active mein kar diya jaaye, yeh teeno structure sahi hote hai aur iss question mein 3rd structure follow ho raha hai.

questions.question:
Change passive to active.
No efforts were seen to have been made by the officials to resolve the crisis.
options: (a) It was seen that officials resolved the crisis.
(b) Officials were seen resolving the crisis effortfully.
(c) The officials seemed to have resolved the crisis.
(d) It was seen that the officials had made no efforts to resolve the crisis.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Sentence mein 'were seen' aur 'to have been made' passive mein hai agar ek bhi verb active mein ho jaaye toh sahi ho jayega kyunki best option nahi hai. Option D chal jayega kyunki 'to have been made' perfect tense ko active mein 'had made' past perfect mein change kar diya meaning ke according, 'were seen' se pata chal raha hai past ka sentence hai, isliye perfect tense ko bhi past perfect mein change kar diya, isliye option D ka structure sahi hoga.

questions.question:
Change passive to active.
A decision has been taken to have the proposal reviewed by an external panel.
options: (a) An external panel has reviewed the proposal.
(b) The proposal is being reviewed by an external panel.
(c) They have decided to get the proposal reviewed by an external panel.
(d) The proposal was reviewed by the panel as per the decision.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c)
Explanation:- Sentence mein 'has been taken' aur 'to have the proposal reviewed' yeh dono passive mein hai aur second verb causative verb ka passive hai, agar inn dono mein ek bhi active ho jaaye toh option sahi maan lenge kyunki best option nahi hai. Option C sahi hoga kyunki 'has been taken' ka active 'have decided' kar diya jo concise version hai 'have taken' ka, isliye 'have decided' bhi sahi hai aur causative verb ke structure ko waisa he chod diya 'to get the proposal reviewed', kyunki ek ko active kiya isliye option C chal jayega/sahi ho jayega.
Best option:- 'They have taken a decision to get/have an external panel to review the proposal'.

questions.question: The [Presiding] Officer walked slowly to the dais.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'officer' noun hai, aur noun ko qualify karne ke liye adjective ka use hota hai, isliye 'presiding' yahan adjective hai.

questions.question: The children were walking [through] the forest.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'through' preposition aur 'the forest' preposition ka object, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: I will wait here [till] he comes.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- 'I will wait' subject + verb hai aur 'he comes' bhi subject + verb hai, aur do clauses ko jodne ka kaam conjunction ka hota hai, isliye 'till' conjunction hai.

questions.question: The son writes [meaningless] letters to his father.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'letters' noun hai jiski visheshta 'meaningless' bata raha hai, noun yaa pronoun ko qualify karne waale ko adjective kehte hai.

questions.question: [Hurrah!] We won the game!
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Interjection'
Explanation:- Wo word jo kisi sudden expression yaa feeling ko bataye unhe interjection kehte hai jaise 'Hurrah!, Alas!, Ouch!, Wow!' etc.

questions.question: [Since] he was late, he missed the train.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- Yahan 'since' do clauses ko jodne ka kaam kar raha hai aur 'kyunki' wala meaning de raha hai, isliye 'since' conjunction hai.

questions.question: Jasmines [and] roses are my favourite flowers.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- Yahan 'and' conjunction hai kyunki 'jasmines' aur 'roses' nouns ko jod raha hai.

questions.question: I will meet you [in] the third week of August.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'in, on, into, above, upon, under, of' etc. yeh prepositions hoti hai, jinke baad preposition ka object ('the third week') aata hai.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: "Their house is not so good as [ours]."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'possessive pronoun'
Explanation:- 'ours' ka matlab 'our house', jo ek noun ki jagah pe aaye aur possession bhi dikhaaye unhe possessive pronoun kehte hai (mine, ours, yours, his, hers, theirs).

questions.question: Rita [eats] her dinner quickly.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'verb'
Explanation:- 'eats' yahan verb hai jiski forms 'eat, ate, eaten, eating' hoti hai.

questions.question: Ravi was declared as the winner in the tie [because] he had hit the most number of fours and sixes.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- 'Ravi was declared' aur 'he had hit' do clauses ko jodne ka kaam 'because' kar raha hai, isliye 'because' conjunction hai.

questions.question: [Hurrah!] What a scintillating beauty the landscape is!
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'interjection'
Explanation:- Wo word jo kisi expression yaa feeling ko bataye unhe interjection kehte hai jaise 'Hurrah!, Alas!, Ouch!, Wow!' etc.

questions.question: The building [is] very ancient.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Intransitive verb'
Explanation:- 'is, am, are, was, were' ke baad koi main verb naa likhi ho toh inhe linking verb (intransitive verb) kehte hai aur 'ancient' adjective (complement) hai.

questions.question: He [has offered] her another chance.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'perfect tense'
Explanation:- 'has offered' present perfect tense hai (has + V3).

questions.question: Identify the non-finite verb: "He tried [to warn] her before leaving."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'infinitive'
Explanation:- 'to + V1' se infinitive banta hai, isliye 'to warn' infinitive hai.

questions.question: [Noticing] the change in the behaviour of the officer, the cadets returned to their position.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'participle'
Explanation:- 'Noticing' yahan present participle (adjective) hai 'the cadets' noun ke liye, isliye 'participle' sahi hoga.

questions.question: [Driven] by hunger, he ate the stale bread.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'past participle'
Explanation:- 'Driven' (V3) yahan past participle hai jo 'he' subject ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: The [most] beautiful actor of the industry was awarded today.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'actor' noun ko 'beautiful' adjective qualify kar raha hai, aur adjective ko qualify karne waale 'most' ko adverb kehte hai.

questions.question: The man in dark blue is the one [who] made us win the match.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'relative pronoun'
Explanation:- 'who, whom, which, that' relative pronouns hote hai jo pronoun + conjunction ka kaam karte hai.

questions.question: He has been working in the Department of Foreign Affairs [since] 2002.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'since' ka yahan meaning 'jabse' hai aur iske baad point of time '2002' object hai, isliye yeh preposition hai.

questions.question: I can [hardly] believe it.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'believe' main verb ko qualify 'hardly' kar raha hai, isliye 'hardly' adverb hai.

questions.question: The ants [fought] the wasps.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'transitive verb'
Explanation:- 'fought' yahan verb hai aur iska object 'the wasps' hai, isliye 'fought' transitive verb hai.

questions.question: I hurt [myself].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'pronoun'
Explanation:- 'myself' yahan reflexive pronoun hai.

questions.question: The Son got [angry] when his father asked the question.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'got' linking verb hai aur linking verb ke baad subject complement 'angry' adjective hai.

questions.question: The flower is [very] beautiful.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'beautiful' adjective hai aur adjective ko qualify 'very' (adverb) kar raha hai.

questions.question: [It] is eleven o'clock now and all of us should retire to bed.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'impersonal pronoun'
Explanation:- 'It' yahan time ('eleven o'clock') ko refer karne wala introductory subject hai, isliye yeh impersonal pronoun hai.

questions.question: He said to him that he was [welcome].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'was' linking verb ke baad 'welcome' yahan subject complement (adjective) hai.

questions.question: This is [his] pen.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'possessive adjective'
Explanation:- 'his' yahan 'pen' noun par possession bana raha hai, isliye 'his' possessive adjective hai.

questions.question: The wonderful [statue] of the leader welcomes all people to the city.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'statue' yahan subject (noun) hai, aur 'wonderful' noun ke liye adjective hai.

questions.question: All the pilgrims rested for a while [under] the banyan tree.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'under' preposition hai aur 'the banyan tree' iska object hai.

questions.question: There was an [exultation] in the group.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'an' article ke baad real subject 'exultation' ek noun hai.

questions.question: Ravi [won] the match with a huge margin.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'transitive verb'
Explanation:- 'won' verb hai aur 'the match' iska object hai, isliye 'won' transitive verb hai.

questions.question: Love your neighbour as [thyself].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'pronoun'
Explanation:- 'thyself' ('yourself' ka archaic रूप) ek reflexive/emphatic pronoun hai.

questions.question: [This] time we woke up to the virus related diseases.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'demonstrative'
Explanation:- 'This' demonstrative adjective hai jo 'time' noun ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: They have been driving [since] early morning.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- Given options mein 'preposition' nahi hai, isliye exam answer key ke according 'adverb' mark kiya jayega.

questions.question: He told me that the teacher [gave] him a pen.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'di-transitive verb'
Explanation:- 'gave' ek di-transitive verb hai jiska indirect object 'him' hai aur direct object 'a pen' hai.

questions.question: The man [who] is in the green shirt is the chief of the day.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'relative pronoun'
Explanation:- 'who' relative pronoun hai jo 'The man' ko refer kar raha hai.

questions.question: [Alas!] He has been defeated.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'interjection'
Explanation:- 'Alas!' dukh express karne wala interjection hai.

questions.question: The [most beautiful] seven monkeys of the landlord were taken for a stroll.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'most beautiful' superlative degree ka adjective hai jo 'monkeys' ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: The preacher said, "No one is [above] the all powerful".
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'above' yahan preposition hai.

questions.question: The secretary [himself] visited the affected families.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'pronoun'
Explanation:- 'himself' yahan emphatic pronoun hai.

questions.question: She [truthfully] answered the detective's questions.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'truthfully' adverb of manner hai jo 'answered' verb ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: He thought the movie ended [abruptly].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'abruptly' adverb of manner hai jo 'ended' verb ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: When he reached the department, the officials [had left] for the meeting.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'past perfect verb'
Explanation:- 'had left' (had + V3) past perfect verb hai.

questions.question: "What is the [latest] news?" asked the Captain.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'latest' adjective hai jo 'news' noun ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: [This] boy is stronger than Ramesh.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'This' demonstrative adjective hai jo 'boy' noun ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: When people found that the jewel was in records of Rahim, they gave [it] to him.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'pronoun'
Explanation:- 'it' yahan pronoun hai jo 'the jewel' ke liye object ban raha hai.

questions.question: He has been living in the jungle for long [and] he knows all the animals here.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'coordinating conjunction'
Explanation:- FANBOYS (For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So) coordinating conjunctions hoti hai.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct adverb of manner:
options: (b) He has just done his work.
(d) He has done his work on my table.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'He does his work carefully'
Explanation:- 'carefully' adverb of manner hai.

questions.question: I know [that] [that] black cow is [his].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'conjunction, demonstrative adjective, possessive pronoun'
Explanation:- First 'that' दो clauses ko jodne wali conjunction hai, second 'that' 'cow' noun ke liye demonstrative adjective hai, aur 'his' bina noun ke aaya possessive pronoun hai.

questions.question: [The] cat loves comfort.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'definite article'
Explanation:- 'a, an' indefinite article hote hai, aur 'the' definite article hota hai.

questions.question: Life is a [solo] fight, and each person makes his or her own journey.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'solo' adjective hai jo 'fight' noun ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: [Being] seriously ill, He was taken to hospital.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'present participle'
Explanation:- 'Being seriously ill' mein 'Being' present participle hai jo 'He' ke liye aaya hai.

questions.question: For the next generation of interior architects and design graduates, work [opportunities] are immense.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'opportunities' subject (noun) hai jiske liye 'are' linking verb aayi hai.

questions.question: Rakesh is [too] old to run fast.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'intensifier'
Explanation:- 'too' 'old' adjective ki intensity badha raha hai, isliye 'intensifier' (adverb of degree) choose karna behtar rahega.

questions.question: I got the news of his [being] arrested.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'gerund'
Explanation:- 'of' preposition hai jiska object 'being' gerund (noun) hai.

questions.question: I know very well [what] you want.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'Relative pronoun'
Explanation:- Yahan 'what' relative pronoun hai jo pronoun + conjunction ka kaam kar raha hai.

questions.question: You are paying [less] attention to your studies these days.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'attention' noun hai jisko qualify 'less' kar raha hai, isliye 'less' adjective hai.

questions.question: Public culture is associated with [extremely] new civil societies.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'intensifier'
Explanation:- 'extremely' adverb of degree (intensifier) hai jo 'new' adjective ki intensity badha raha hai.

questions.question: We went away [after] they had left.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- 'after' yahan conjunction hai jo 'We went away' aur 'they had left' do clauses ko jod raha hai.

questions.question: They wandered [around] aimlessly.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'around' ke baad koi object (noun) nahi hai balki yeh 'wandered' verb ko qualify kar raha hai, isliye yahan 'around' adverb hai.

questions.question: The conclusions that they came to are highly [questionable].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'are' linking verb hai aur 'questionable' subject complement (adjective) hai.

questions.question: This year marks the [quincentenary] of Columbus's voyage to America.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Noun'
Explanation:- 'the' article ke baad 'quincentenary' (500th anniversary) noun hai.

questions.question: I still cherish the memories of those [far-off] days.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'days' noun ko qualify 'far-off' kar raha hai, isliye 'far-off' adjective hai.

questions.question: I don't think I'll come on Saturday. I have a lot of work to do. [Besides], I don't really like parties.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'Besides' sentence ke starting mein comma ke sath poore sentence ko modify kar raha hai, isliye yahan adverb hai.

questions.question: The [bottom line] is that we have to make a decision today.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'The' article ke baad 'bottom line' subject (noun) hai.

questions.question: Try to knock that vase [over].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'knock over' phrasal verb mein 'over' ke baad koi object nahi hai, isliye 'over' yahan adverb particle hai.

questions.question: I'd like an ice cream. Will you have [one] too?
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'pronoun'
Explanation:- 'one' yahan 'an ice cream' noun ki jagah aaya pronoun hai.

questions.question: My parents lent me the money. [Otherwise], I could not have afforded the trip.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'Otherwise' sentence ke starting mein comma lagake poore sentence ko qualify kar raha hai (conjunctive adverb).

questions.question: She wrote me an [anguished] letter from her prison cell.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'anguished' yahan 'letter' noun ko qualify kar raha hai, isliye adjective hai.

questions.question: There is [a] visitor for you.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'indefinite article'
Explanation:- 'a, an' indefinite article hote hai.

questions.question: He headed the Indian freedom struggle [which] paved the way for non violent struggle for other countries in the 20th century.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'relative pronoun'
Explanation:- 'which' relative pronoun hai jo 'the Indian freedom struggle' ko refer kar raha hai.

questions.question: [Where] there is peace for some time, there will be prosperity.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'Where' yahan place bata raha hai (relative adverb of place).

questions.question: [Alas!] We have been defeated.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'interjection'
Explanation:- 'Alas!' dukh ya shok prakat karne wala interjection hai.

questions.question: A zero is a [zero] always.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'a' article ke baad 'zero' subject complement (noun) hai.

questions.question: When we entered his home, we saw him [sleeping] on the floor.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'present participle'
Explanation:- 'saw' verb ke object 'him' ke baad 'sleeping' present participle (object complement) ki tarah kaam kar raha hai.

questions.question: The lake is one of the most [beautiful] ones in the country.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'beautiful' adjective hai jo 'ones' pronoun ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: [Honesty] is the best policy.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'uncountable noun'
Explanation:- 'Honesty' ek abstract noun hota hai, jise uncountable noun ki category mein rakhte hai.

questions.question: There is many a slip [between] the cup and the lip.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'between' yahan preposition hai aur 'the cup and the lip' iske objects hai.

questions.question: Ravi and Megha reached first, [but] Guha and Saavi finished third.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- 'but' coordinating conjunction hai jo do clauses ko jod raha hai.

questions.question: He is [the] most sought after teacher in the school.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'determiner'
Explanation:- Articles ('a, an, the') determiners ki category mein aate hai.

questions.question: She sings [much] better than I do.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'better' comparative adverb ko qualify karne wala 'much' bhi adverb hai.

questions.question: The story was in all the [dailies].
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'the' article ke baad 'dailies' (daily newspapers) plural noun hai.

questions.question: [Smoking] is injurious to health.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'gerund'
Explanation:- 'Smoking' yahan 'is' verb ka subject (gerund/verbal noun) hai.

questions.question: What made you choose this [one] rather than the other?
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'pronoun'
Explanation:- 'this' demonstrative adjective ke baad 'one' pronoun hai.

questions.question: There is still [some] water in the bottle.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'determiner'
Explanation:- 'some' yahan 'water' noun ke liye determiner (quantifier) hai.

questions.question: I have already told you that you [need] not come tomorrow.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'auxiliary verb'
Explanation:- 'need not come' mein 'need' ke baad 'not' aur bare infinitive 'come' hai, isliye 'need' modal auxiliary verb hai.

questions.question: [Having finished] her work, Sharmila left home at 8:00 p.m.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'perfect participle'
Explanation:- 'Having + V3' ('Having finished') ke structure ko perfect participle kehte hai.

questions.question: My teacher always moves [around] in her class while teaching.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'adverb'
Explanation:- 'around' yahan adverb hai jo 'moves' verb ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: The [cantankerous] men of the town roar around the marketplace.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'cantankerous' (jhgadalu/bad-tempered) qualitative adjective hai jo 'men' noun ko qualify kar raha hai.

questions.question: India is revered as the [fountainhead] of democracy in the world today.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'noun'
Explanation:- 'the' definite article ke baad 'fountainhead' (source/origin) noun hai.

questions.question: She got angry and asked him [to go] away. Here infinitive is acting as?
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'object'
Explanation:- 'asked' di-transitive verb ka indirect object 'him' hai aur 'to go' (infinitive) direct object hai.

questions.question: [Having slept] for 8 hours, he started his journey again.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'perfect participle'
Explanation:- 'Having + V3' ('Having slept') perfect participle hota hai.

questions.question: When he saw his father, he started [studying] Mathematics.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'gerund'
Explanation:- 'started' verb ka object 'studying' gerund (verbal noun) hai.

questions.question: [In spite of] having high fever Radhika kept doing her task.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'preposition'
Explanation:- 'In spite of' compound preposition hota hai jiska object 'having' gerund hai.

questions.question: He will help you financially [provided] you return the money on time.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- 'provided' (basharte/if) conditional conjunction hai jo do clauses ko jod raha hai.

questions.question: Call me [in case] there is any problem.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'conjunction'
Explanation:- 'in case' yahan conjunction hai jo do clauses ko jod raha hai.

questions.question: They are used to [travelling] in trains.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'gerund'
Explanation:- 'be used to' mein 'to' preposition hota hai aur 'travelling' preposition ka object (gerund) hai.

questions.question: He claims [to have scored] 90% marks in the exam.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d) Correct answer is 'perfect infinitive'
Explanation:- 'to + have + V3' ('to have scored') ke structure ko perfect infinitive kehte hai.

questions.question: He felt [lonely] when his friends went to the party without him.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'adjective'
Explanation:- 'felt' linking verb ke baad 'lonely' subject complement (adjective) hai.

questions.question: Her eyes shone like stars in the night.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Simile'
Explanation:- Kisi cheez ka comparison 'like, as' lagake kare, toh usse 'Simile' kehte hai.

questions.question: The phone screamed for attention.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'Personification'
Explanation:- Non-human cheez ('phone') ko human quality ('screamed') dene ko Personification kehte hai.

questions.question: The silence was so loud, it hurt my ears.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Oxymoron'
Explanation:- Jab do opposite ideas/words ('silence' aur 'loud') sath mein aayein toh Oxymoron hota hai.

questions.question: The clouds wept all day.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Personification'
Explanation:- Non-human cheez ('clouds') ko human quality ('wept') dene ko Personification kehte hai.

questions.question: The athlete is a cheetah on the track.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Metaphor'
Explanation:- Kisi cheez ka direct comparison bina 'like, as' ke kare toh wo Metaphor hota hai.

questions.question: The cake is as soft as cotton.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Simile'
Explanation:- Yahan cake ka comparison cotton se 'as...as' lagake kiya hai, isliye yeh Simile hoga.

questions.question: He kicked the bucket last year.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Euphemism'
Explanation:- 'kicked the bucket' ka matlab 'mar jaana' (died), kisi harsh baat ko halke tarike se kehne ko Euphemism kehte hai.

questions.question: The kettle hissed as the water boiled.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Onomatopoeia'
Explanation:- Wo word jo sound ko imitate kare ('hissed') unhe Onomatopoeia kehte hai.

questions.question: Why do we drive on parkways and park on driveways?
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'Pun'
Explanation:- Pun ka matlab hai words ke sath play karna ('drive on parkways and park on driveways').

questions.question: The waves crashed angrily against the shore.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Personification'
Explanation:- Non-human 'waves' ko human emotion 'angrily' dena Personification hai.

questions.question: He is as strong as an ox.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Simile'
Explanation:- 'as strong as an ox' mein 'as...as' se comparison ho raha hai, isliye Simile hai.

questions.question: The car coughed and spluttered before stopping.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Personification'
Explanation:- Non-human 'car' ko human action 'coughed' dena Personification hai.

questions.question: He runs faster than a speeding bullet.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Hyperbole'
Explanation:- Baat ko bahut badha-chadha kar (exaggerate karke) kaha gaya hai, isliye Hyperbole hoga.

questions.question: The pen is mightier than the sword.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Metaphor'
Explanation:- Yahan 'pen' aur 'sword' ka symbolic/metaphorical comparison ho raha hai.

questions.question: The teacher gave me mountains of homework.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Hyperbole'
Explanation:- 'mountains of homework' exaggeration (badha-chadha kar kehna) hai, isliye Hyperbole hoga.

questions.question: The doorbell went ding-dong.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Onomatopoeia'
Explanation:- 'ding-dong' sound word hai, isliye Onomatopoeia hoga.

questions.question: He has been called to heaven.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Euphemism'
Explanation:- Death ki baat ko polite/gentle way ('called to heaven') mein kaha gaya hai, isliye Euphemism hoga.

questions.question: She sells shiny seashells on Sundays.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Alliteration'
Explanation:- Consonant sound 's/sh' ka bar-bar repetition ho raha hai, isliye Alliteration kehte hai.

questions.question: He's in between jobs right now.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Euphemism'
Explanation:- 'in between jobs' berozgar (unemployed) kehne ka polite tarika hai, isliye Euphemism hoga.

questions.question: The snake slithered silently.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'Alliteration'
Explanation:- 's' consonant sound ka repetition ('snake slithered silently') Alliteration hai.

questions.question: The baby's laugh was like music.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Simile'
Explanation:- 'like' lagakar comparison kiya gaya hai, isliye Simile hoga.

questions.question: Her words cut deeper than a knife.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'Metaphor'
Explanation:- Bina 'like/as' ke words ko knife se compare kiya gaya hai, isliye Metaphor hoga.

questions.question: Life is a puzzle, each piece matters.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b) Correct answer is 'Metaphor'
Explanation:- 'Life' ko direct 'a puzzle' bataya gaya hai bina 'like/as' ke, isliye Metaphor hoga.

questions.question: The birds chirped cheerfully in the morning.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Onomatopoeia'
Explanation:- 'chirped' birds ki sound ko imitate karne wala word hai, isliye Onomatopoeia hoga.

questions.question: He was buried in paperwork.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Hyperbole'
Explanation:- 'buried in paperwork' bahut jyada kaam ko exaggerate karke batana hai, isliye Hyperbole hoga.

questions.question: The stars winked at us from the sky.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Personification'
Explanation:- Non-human 'stars' ko human action 'winked' dena Personification hai.

questions.question: The customer service was painfully pleasant.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c) Correct answer is 'Oxymoron'
Explanation:- 'painfully pleasant' do opposite words ek sath likhe hain, isliye Oxymoron kahenge.

questions.question: I'm on a seafood diet. I see food, and I eat it.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Pun'
Explanation:- 'seafood' aur 'see food' words ke sound se play kiya gaya hai, isliye Pun hoga.

questions.question: The mountains stood tall, watching over the valley.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Personification'
Explanation:- Non-human 'mountains' ko 'watching over' human quality dena Personification hai.

questions.question: He calls himself a warrior and he is afraid of fighting.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a) Correct answer is 'Irony'
Explanation:- Expected outcome ka ulta hona (khud ko warrior kehna par fighting se darna) Irony kehlata hai.

questions.question: She said she was seeing her brother the following day.
options: (a) She said, "I am seeing my brother tomorrow."
(b) She says, "I will see my brother tomorrow."
(c) She said, "I was seeing my brother tomorrow."
(d) She said, "I should see my brother tomorrow."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Indirect mein 'was seeing' past continuous hai, toh direct ke present continuous ('I am seeing') se aaya hoga aur 'the following day' 'tomorrow' se, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: She said, "I have finished my work."
options: (a) She said that she had finished her work.
(b) She said that she would finish her work.
(c) She said that she will finish her work.
(d) She said that she has finished her work.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'have finished' present perfect hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had finished') mein change ho jata hai, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: She said to me, "I shall come to meet you tomorrow."
options: (a) She asked me that could she come to meet me the next day.
(b) She tells me that she could come to meet me tomorrow.
(c) She told me that she will come to meet me tomorrow.
(d) She told me that she would come to meet me the next day.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- 'shall' indirect speech mein 'would' mein aur 'tomorrow' 'the next day' mein change ho jata hai, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: She said that she could bake cookies.
options: (a) She had said, "I can bake cookies."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- 'could' indirect mein hai, toh direct mein 'can' se aaya hoga, aur reporting verb 'said' rahegi, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: He said, "I have finished my homework."
options: (a) He said that he had to finish his homework.
(b) He said that he has finished his homework.
(c) He said that he would finish his homework.
(d) He said that he had finished his homework.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'have finished' present perfect hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had finished') mein change ho jata hai, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: Ron said to me, "He had his lunch at 2 p.m. yesterday."
options: (a) Ron told me that he ate his lunch at 2 p.m. the previous day.
(b) Ron told me that he had had his lunch at 2 p.m. the previous day.
(c) Ron told me that he had his lunch at 2 p.m. the previous day.
(d) Ron told me that he had eaten his lunch at 2 p.m. the previous day.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'had' (V2, past indefinite) diya hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had had') mein change ho jayega, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: The child says, "I do not want to go to school."
options: (a) The child say that I do not want to go to school.
(b) The child says that I do not want to go to school.
(c) The child says that he do not want to go to school.
(d) The child says that he does not want to go to school.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Direct mein reporting verb 'says' present ki lagi hai, isliye tense mein koi change nahi hoga aur 'I do' child ke according 'he does' mein change hoga, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: Sakshi said that she would do it then or never.
options: (a) Sakshi said, "I would do it then or never."
(b) Sakshi said, "I have to do it now or never."
(c) Sakshi said, "I will do it now or never."
(d) Sakshi said, "I will do it then or never."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c)
Explanation:- Indirect mein 'would' direct ke 'will' se aur 'then' direct ke 'now' se aaya hoga, isliye 'I will do it now or never' wala option C sahi hoga.

questions.question: Jatin said, "I was at home yesterday."
options: (a) Jatin said that he was at home yesterday.
(b) Jatin said that he had been at home the day before.
(c) Jatin said he was at home the day before.
(d) Jatin said he was at home.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'was' past indefinite hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had been') aur 'yesterday' 'the day before' mein change hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: "I am not feeling well," said Mary.
options: (a) Mary says that she is not feeling well.
(b) Mary said that she is not feeling well.
(c) Mary says that she wasn't feeling well.
(d) Mary said that she was not feeling well.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'am not feeling' present continuous hai, toh indirect mein past continuous ('was not feeling') mein change hoga, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: He exclaimed with delight that he had won the first prize.
options: (a) "Wow! I might win the first prize," said he.
(b) "Hurrah! I have won the first prize," said he.
(c) "Hurrah! I win the first prize," said he.
(d) "Hurrah! I will win the first prize," said he.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Indirect mein 'had won' past perfect hai, toh direct mein present perfect ('have won') se aaya hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: Gita said, "I lost my umbrella."
options: (a) Gita said that I lost my umbrella.
(b) Gita said that she had lost her umbrella.
(c) Gita expressed that she has lost her umbrella.
(d) Gita told me that he lost her umbrella.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'lost' past indefinite diya hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had lost') mein change hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: Ritu said, "I am eating apples."
options: (a) Ritu said that she was eating apples.
(b) Ritu said that she has been eating apples.
(c) Ritu told that she was eating apples.
(d) Ritu said that she had been eating apples.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'am eating' present continuous diya hai, toh indirect mein past continuous ('was eating') aur 'said' rahega, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: My father said, "Neha shall come back by 3:00 p.m."
options: (a) My father said that Neha should come back by 3:00 p.m.
(b) My father told that Neha should come back by 3:00 p.m.
(c) My father told that Neha shall come back by 3:00 p.m.
(d) My father said that Neha will come back by 3:00 p.m.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'shall' diya hai, toh indirect mein 'should' aur reporting verb 'said' rahegi, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: He said, "I can't attend the meeting tomorrow."
options: (a) He said that he couldn't attend the meeting tomorrow.
(b) He said that he couldn't attend the meeting the next day.
(c) He said that he can't attend the meeting tomorrow.
(d) He said that he can't attend the meeting the next day.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'can't' indirect mein 'couldn't' aur 'tomorrow' 'the next day' mein change hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: The Minister explained that he was working for the benefit of the country.
options: (a) The Minister explains, "I will work for the benefit of the country."
(b) The Minister explained, "I am working for the benefit of the country."
(c) The Minister explained, "He was working for the benefit of the country."
(d) The Minister explained, "I was working for the benefit of the country."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Indirect mein 'was working' past continuous hai, toh direct ke present continuous ('I am working') se aaya hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: He promised, "He will not do the mistake again."
options: (a) He promised that he would not do the mistake next time.
(b) He promised that he would not did the mistake next time.
(c) He promised that he will not do the mistake again.
(d) He promises that he will not do the mistake again.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'will not do' diya hai, toh indirect mein 'would not do' mein change hoga, joki option A mein follow ho raha hai.

questions.question: Bajrang said, "I went to Chandigarh yesterday."
options: (a) Bajrang said that he had gone to Chandigarh the day before.
(b) Bajrang said that he was gone to Chandigarh the day before.
(c) Bajrang said that he gone to Chandigarh the day before.
(d) Bajrang said that he have gone to Chandigarh the day before.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'went' past indefinite diya hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had gone') aur 'yesterday' 'the day before' mein change hoga, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: He said, "My mother will be here tomorrow."
options: (a) He said that his mother would be there the next day.
(b) He said that his mother would be here tomorrow.
(c) He said that my mother will be here the next day.
(d) He said that my mother will be here tomorrow.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'will be here tomorrow' indirect mein 'would be there the next day' mein change ho jayega, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: Ram said, "I watched football."
options: (a) Ram said that I shall watch football.
(b) Ram said that he had watched football.
(c) Ram said that they watched football.
(d) Ram said that he watches football.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'watched' past indefinite hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('had watched') mein change hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: He said, "I am going to the party tonight."
options: (a) He said that he would go to the party that night.
(b) He said that he was going to the party tonight.
(c) He said that he was going to the party that night.
(d) He said that he is going to the party tonight.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'am going' indirect mein 'was going' aur 'tonight' 'that night' mein change hoga, isliye option C sahi hoga.

questions.question: She said, "I cannot call you at this time."
options: (a) She said that she could not call me at that time.
(b) She said that she cannot call me at that time.
(c) She said that she would not call me at this time.
(d) She said that she could not call me this time.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'cannot call you at this time' indirect mein 'could not call me at that time' mein change ho jayega, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: Rohan said, "I will arrive late."
options: (a) Rohan says that he is late in his arrival.
(b) Rohan said that he would arrive late.
(c) Rohan said that I will arrive late.
(d) Rohan said that he is arriving late.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (b)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'will arrive' indirect mein 'would arrive' mein change hoga, isliye option B sahi hoga.

questions.question: Rathan said, "I have written a poem."
options: (a) Rathan said that he has written a poem.
(b) Rathan said that he wrote a poem.
(c) Rathan said that I had written a poem.
(d) Rathan said that he had written a poem.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'have written' present perfect hai, toh indirect mein past perfect ('he had written') mein change hoga, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: Mohan said, "I shall go as soon as it is possible."
options: (a) Mohan said that he would go as soon as it is possible.
(b) Mohan said that he will go as soon as it is possible.
(c) Mohan said that he would go as soon as it was possible.
(d) Mohan said that he will go as soon as it was possible.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (c)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'shall' aur 'it is possible' indirect mein 'would' aur 'it was possible' mein change hoga, isliye option C sahi hoga.

questions.question: He said that it would be fun if I could join.
options: (a) He said, "It will be fun if you can join."
(b) He said, "It will have been fun if you had joined."
(c) He said, "It will have been fun if I could have joined."
(d) He said, "It will have been fun if I had joined."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Indirect speech mein 'would be fun' aur 'could' direct mein 'will be fun' aur 'can' se aaya hoga, isliye option A sahi hoga.

questions.question: The teacher informed that the exam had been postponed.
options: (a) The teacher informs, "The exam had been postponed."
(b) The teacher informed, "The exam was being postponed."
(c) The teacher informs, "The exam has been postponed."
(d) The teacher informed, "The exam has been postponed."
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Indirect speech mein 'had been postponed' direct ke 'has been postponed' se aaya hoga aur reporting verb 'informed' rahegi, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: He said, "I shall need a copy of the documents."
options: (a) He said that he will need a copy of the documents.
(b) He said that he shall need a copy of the document.
(c) He said that he is going to need a copy of the document.
(d) He said that he would need a copy of the documents.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'shall' diya hai, toh indirect mein 'would' mein change hoga, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: Raju said to Reghu, "Stay back."
options: (a) Raju ordered Reghu to stay back.
(b) Raju had ordered Reghu to stay back.
(c) Raju orders Reghu to stay back.
(d) Raju has ordered Reghu to stay back.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Direct speech imperative hai aur reporting verb past ('said to') mein hai, isliye 'Raju ordered Reghu to stay back' (option A) sahi hoga.

questions.question: "I am playing the keyboard," she explained.
options: (a) She explained that she is playing the keyboard.
(b) She said that she had been playing the keyboard.
(c) She said that she is playing the keyboard.
(d) She explained that she was playing the keyboard.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (d)
Explanation:- Direct mein 'am playing' present continuous hai, toh indirect mein past continuous ('was playing') mein change hoga, isliye option D sahi hoga.

questions.question: They said that they had been waiting for the bus for over an hour.
options: (a) "We have been waiting for the bus for over an hour," they said.
(b) "We waited for the bus for over an hour," they said.
(c) "We had waited for the bus for over an hour," they said.
(d) "We are waiting for the bus for over an hour," they said.
questions.solutionHinglish:
Ans (a)
Explanation:- Indirect mein 'had been waiting' aur 'for over an hour' duration di hai, toh direct mein present perfect continuous ('have been waiting') wala option A sahi hoga.
